_readme: Every knob the grant agent obeys. Setup copies this to settings.json and fills it from the client's answers. run.sh turns it into the instructions for each run. Full docs: README.md#settings.

run._drafts_note: Drafts are packages the agent writes but does not submit: federal and state applications, letters of inquiry, anything in approve mode. They cost the client review time, so they are capped separately.
run._cycle_note: Most programs accept one application per business per cycle (a month, a round, a year). The agent checks applications/, data/queue.md and logs/grants-log.md before every application.
run._deadline_note: A web form closing in under 2 days is still worth submitting. A federal or foundation package needs the client's review, signatures and attachments, so anything closing in under 14 days is logged as too tight instead of drafted.

submission._mode_note: auto: scheduled runs submit simple web-form grants (Tier A in config/spec.md) that clear every gate. approve: scheduled runs draft; every application waits as READY FOR APPROVAL until the owner clicks 'Approve for sending' on the dashboard, and the next run sends it. Federal, state and package grants (Tier B) are never submitted by the agent in either mode.
submission._checkbox_note: A checkbox like 'I certify this information is accurate' may be ticked, because every fact on the form comes from the client's confirmed files. false: any such checkbox makes the application NEEDS HUMAN.
submission._signature_note: A typed or drawn signature is the client signing for the business. Off by default: the form is filled, left open, and logged NEEDS HUMAN.
submission._fee_note: Legitimate grants rarely charge to apply. 0 means any fee sends the grant to the FOR YOU list with the fee amount; the agent never enters payment details.

targets._apply_as_note: Which entities in profile.json to find grants for: business, nonprofit, or both. A nonprofit grant needs an enabled nonprofit entity with IRS status (or a fiscal sponsor the program accepts). The agent never applies as one entity using the other's facts.
targets._keywords_note: Used for the Grants.gov search and the web-search lane. Setup writes these from what the client does and what the money is for.
targets._vote_note: Some 'grants' are popularity contests decided by public votes. false: they go to the FOR YOU list, because winning one takes the client's own promotion.
targets.fit_note: One or two sentences, in the client's words, about what money is worth chasing. The agent uses this as a judgment gate. Example: 'Grants that pay for equipment, training or marketing. Skip anything under $2,000 that needs more than an hour of writing.'

federal._agencies_note: Optional Grants.gov agency codes to restrict the search (e.g. SBA, DOC, USDA). Empty searches every agency.

channels._signed_in_portals_note: Grant portals where the CLIENT created the account and Chrome is signed in (Submittable, Hello Alice, a foundation's own portal). The agent may apply inside that session. It never creates an account or types a password; a login page is NEEDS HUMAN.
channels._never_submit_note: Federal submissions are signed by the client's Authorized Organization Representative. The agent drafts the package and the client submits it.
channels._source_only_note: Aggregators are for finding grants. The agent always applies on the funder's own page.

documents._narrative_note: Used only when a question gives no limit. When the form states a word or character limit, that limit wins. Rules: config/documents.md.

integrations._post_run_note: Optional path to a python3 script run after each scheduled run, e.g. one that emails the client the run summary. Empty by default.
